newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan slightly lifts veil on nuclear shipment.
newsitem.headline: Japan slightly lifts veil on nuclear shipment.

text.p: In a rare disclosure of advance information about a nuclear shipment, Japan Nuclear Fuel Ltd said on Friday it expects to start unloading about 600 tonnes of uranium at Mutsuogawara port in northern Japan on Tuesday.
It said in a statement that the uranium was on its way from France and would be unloaded at the port between Tuesday and Thursday.

The firm's operations include uranium enrichment and disposal of low-level radioactive fuel. It is also constructing a reprocessing plant. The uranium -- the largest volume ever transported in one shipment -- will be used at facilities in Rokkashomura, Aomori Prefecture, close to Mutsuogawara port.
Japan has cited security reasons for its refusal to disclose shipment schedules, including dates and routes, despite strident calls to do so by anti-nuclear campaigners.
Friday's disclosure -- less than a week before the ship is due to arrive -- was made after talks with the Science and Technology Agency, a spokesman at Japan Nuclear Fuel said.
He could not say for certain, however, whether or how much advance information would be released on future shipments.

A little over 70 percent of Japan Nuclear Fuel's capital is jointly held by Japan's nine main utility companies and Japan Atomic Power Co, which was established by the utilities and manufacturers for the development, construction and operation of nuclear power plants.
